figures.caption: Figure 1: Illustration of the three temporal dynamics schemes used in this study. Three image regions with high, intermediate, and low normalized input intensity are shown from top to bottom. Rate dynamics represents input magnitude through spike frequency, such that stronger inputs generate denser spike trains. Poisson-Burst dynamics generates stochastic bursts at discrete temporal intervals, where stronger inputs increase the probability of burst occurrence and the number of spikes within each triggered burst is sampled from a Poisson distribution. Delayed-Burst dynamics represents input magnitude primarily through burst latency, where stronger inputs produce earlier burst onset and weaker inputs produce later responses. Each Delayed-Burst event contains a fixed number of spikes with a fixed inter-spike interval.

Figure 2: MIA framework using three shadow models. Three shadow models with the same architecture are independently trained using separate shadow train/test splits. For each shadow model, representations obtained from its training samples are labeled as members (IN ), while representations obtained from its held-out test samples are labeled as non-members (OUT ). The outputs from all three shadow models are pooled to construct a larger attack training set. The target model is queried in the same manner to construct the attack test set, and the trained attack model predicts whether each target sample belongs to the target model’s training set.
Figure 3: (a) Utility and (b) Privacy under homogeneous temporal dynamics. Bars show the threerun mean, and shaded regions indicate ±1 standard deviation.

Figure 4: Classification performance under homogeneous Rate dynamics and heterogeneous inputlevel temporal configurations across MNIST, F-MNIST, Iris, and Breast Cancer. Configuration labels indicate the fraction of input dimensions assigned to each temporal dynamic. For example, 90R/10PB denotes 90% Rate and 10% Poisson-Burst dynamics, while 80R/10PB/10DB denotes 80% Rate, 10% Poisson-Burst, and 10% Delayed-Burst dynamics.
Figure 5: Membership-inference vulnerability under homogeneous Rate dynamics and heterogeneous input-level temporal configurations across MNIST, F-MNIST, Iris, and Breast Cancer.

Figure 6: Illustration of temporal jitter applied to Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst spike trains. Selected spikes are shifted by one timestep (±1), while the overall spike pattern and spike count are preserved.
Figure 7: Classification utility under increasing temporal jitter for Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst dynamics.
Figure 8: Membership-inference vulnerability under increasing temporal jitter for Rate, PoissonBurst, and Delayed-Burst dynamics.
Figure 9: Classification utility under increasing input noise for Rate, Poisson-Burst, and DelayedBurst dynamics on MNIST, F-MNIST, and Breast Cancer.
Figure 10: Membership-inference vulnerability under increasing input noise for Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst dynamics on MNIST, F-MNIST, and Breast Cancer.
Figure 11: Classification utility under increasing spike noise for Rate, Poisson-Burst, and DelayedBurst dynamics on MNIST, F-MNIST, and Breast Cancer.
Figure 12: Membership-inference vulnerability under increasing spike noise for Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst dynamics on MNIST, F-MNIST, and Breast Cancer.

Figure 13: Representative AdEx spike rasters for the Burst and Delayed-Burst configurations. The Burst setting produces temporally clustered spike activity, whereas the Delayed-Burst setting shifts concentrated firing to later time steps and results in sparser activation.
Figure 14: Classification utility of LIF and AdEx neurons under Rate, Burst, and Delayed-Burst temporal dynamics on (a) MNIST, (b) F-MNIST, (c) CIFAR-10, (d) Iris, and (e) Breast Cancer.

Figure 15: Membership-inference vulnerability (MIA AUC) of LIF and AdEx neurons under Rate, Burst, and Delayed-Burst temporal dynamics on (a) MNIST, (b) F-MNIST, (c) CIFAR-10, (d) Iris, and (e) Breast Cancer. Lower values indicate reduced leakage.
Figure 16: Classification utility of SNNs trained with evolutionary learning and backpropagation under Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst temporal dynamics on (a) Iris and (b) Breast Cancer.

Figure 17: Membership-inference vulnerability of SNNs trained with evolutionary learning and backpropagation under Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst temporal dynamics on (a) Iris and (b) Breast Cancer.

Figure 18: Classification performance of Rate, Poisson-Burst, and Delayed-Burst temporal dynamics under increasing DPSGD privacy budgets on (a) MNIST and (b) F-MNIST. Solid lines show test accuracy as ϵ increases, while dashed lines indicate the corresponding non-private baseline accuracy for each temporal dynamic.
